I’m using the repository’s `crimes-codebase-risk` workflow because this is a refactor proposal driven by `crimes scan`. I’ll confirm the scan and inspect the three implementations so the proposed API preserves their actual differences.

The global `crimes` binary is not installed in this environment, so I’m treating the supplied JSON as the authoritative scan result and validating it against the source. The three sanitizer bodies are behaviorally identical; only exported names and local variable names differ. One important wrinkle: the nearby admin helpers are not semantically equivalent and should not be folded into the sanitizer refactor.

The scan confirms one medium-confidence near-duplicate across all three sanitizers:

- `sanitizeUserInput` in `src/sanitize-a.ts`
- `sanitizeText` in `src/sanitize-b.ts`
- `cleanMessage` in `src/sanitize-c.ts`

Their behavior is identical; only identifiers differ.

Proposed refactor: add a shared module with one canonical API:

```ts
// src/sanitize.ts
export function sanitizeText(input: string | null | undefined): string;
```

The implementation should contain the existing normalization and rejection pipeline unchanged. No options are needed because there are no behavioral differences to parameterize.

Files affected:

- Add [sanitize.ts](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/06-stress-duplication/src/sanitize.ts) with the consolidated implementation.
- Change [sanitize-a.ts](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/06-stress-duplication/src/sanitize-a.ts) so `sanitizeUserInput` delegates to `sanitizeText`.
- Change [sanitize-b.ts](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/06-stress-duplication/src/sanitize-b.ts) to re-export or delegate to the shared function.
- Change [sanitize-c.ts](/Users/andrew/dev/crimes/evals/fixtures/06-stress-duplication/src/sanitize-c.ts) so `cleanMessage` delegates to it.
- Add or update sanitizer tests to cover nullish input, whitespace/control characters, length limiting, rejected prefixes, punctuation, and uppercase normalization.

Compatibility wrappers can preserve the existing exports:

```ts
export const sanitizeUserInput = sanitizeText;
export { sanitizeText };
export const cleanMessage = sanitizeText;
```

The `assertAdminA/B/C` functions should remain separate for now: despite the related policy finding, they have different semantics (`admin`, `admin || owner`, and `not admin`) and cannot safely share one boolean helper without first clarifying their intended policies. The telemetry duplication is also a separate refactor.
